transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Lina Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Atlas Health - Lead ML Eng), Tom Baker (Atlas - Platform Eng), Maya Ortiz (Atlas - PM)

Summary: quick follow-up after last week's POC outage where customers saw intermittent 5xx and client timeouts. Goal: align on root cause evidence, short term mitigations, and testing plan.

[00:00] Lina (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick roll call, we got Marcus here from our infra team, and then Atlas team?
[00:07] Priya (Atlas): yep that's us, Priya, Tom and Maya on call.
[00:10] Lina: great, last week we saw the spike of 5xxs around 14:30 UTC, Marcus took point on triage, Marcus can you summarize what you found?
[00:18] Marcus (Redwood SE): yeah, yeah so we looked at the traces and initial thing is there was a small window where the KV cache thrash and some requests fell back to cold path which bumped latency, some of the requests then timed out at the client and produced 502/504 depending on the proxy, also we saw a couple internal timeouts in the model runtime leading to 5xx. not all requests, it was more like a fraction, roughly 0.8-1.5% of requests during the spike.
[00:43] Tom (Atlas): ek that aligns with what we saw, our retry logic hit and we got a bunch of duplicate requests, which probably made the burst worse. we use default client retry of 3 attempts.
[00:56] Maya (Atlas): and it impacted our user journeys for about 20 minutes, so product people are asking for concrete fixes.
[01:03] Priya: just to add the p95 latency spiked to 1.8s and our timeout is set to 2s on the frontend, so when the backend did 2s+ we started seeing 504s.
[01:11] Lina: ok so two threads: one is backend tail latency/5xx root cause, second is retry and client-side timeouts amplifying the burst.
[01:20] Marcus: exactly, and we also saw some rate limit responses in the logs around the same time — not a hard reject but 429s for a small subset which then retried and again contributed.
[01:30] Tom: can you clarify where rate limiting is applied? is that Redwood edge or our proxy?
[01:35] Marcus: it's a mix — we have token-based per-customer soft limits on the Redwood side, and there's also your ingress and the CDN which may have config, so multiple layers.
[01:45] Priya: got it. is there anything obvious we should change on our side right now to reduce blast radius?
[01:50] Lina: short term i'd suggest increasing client timeout to 5s and add jitter to retries and also we can do a temporary rate bump on our POC quota for 48 hours while we run tests.
[01:59] Priya: increasing timeout to 5s might be ok, but curious if that just masks the problem.
[02:04] Marcus: it's a band-aid, yes, but it reduces immediate user errors while we root cause. also tuning backoff to exponential with jitter reduces thundering herd.
[02:13] Tom: ok on the backoff, we can change that today. do you have example settings?
[02:19] Marcus: yes i'll paste recommended settings — initial 100ms, multiplier 2.0, max 2s, jitter 20-50%. i'll add them to the shared deck.
[02:28] Maya: what's your suggestion about the KV cache? if it's thrashing maybe we need bigger cache or pinning?
[02:33] Marcus: pinning hot prefixes for the POC helps; also we can bump cache memory config on the serving nodes for the POC environment, it's a config change and we can do it behind the scenes.
[02:42] Priya: timeline for that?
[02:44] Marcus: i can do a config change and monitor within a few hours, but i'll want to run a short smoke test first.
[02:50] Lina: another question — do you have the correlation IDs from the 2026-03-19 window? those will help us map traces end-to-end.
[02:57] Priya: yes we do, we dumped some logs but not sure if timestamps matched, i'll send them.
[03:03] Marcus: perfect, once we have correlation IDs we can join our traces and identify if the runtime produced 5xx or it was the edge/proxy.
[03:10] Priya: note there's a small chance it's our k8s ingress; we've seen occasional 502s when the ingress backend times out, so we'll check our side too.
[03:17] Tom: speaking of rate limits, can Redwood temporarily increase our POC quota? that would let us run the spike tests without 429s.
[03:24] Lina: yes we can do a temporary 2x increase for 48 hours, we'll monitor and then revert. we'll also provide guidance on safe spike tests.
[03:31] Maya: thanks, that helps.
[03:33] Lina: ok next — monitoring: Marcus, what dashboards should we watch?
[03:37] Marcus: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, 429 rate, cache hit ratio, and model runtime CPU/GPU stalls. i'll share a dashboard link.
[03:45] Priya: can we get an alert threshold recommendation?
[03:48] Marcus: set alert if 5xx > 0.5% for 5 minutes or if p95 > 1s sustained for 5 minutes, and 429 > 1% for 5 minutes. these are starting points.
[03:58] Tom: good. also can we get the raw request/response payloads for a few failed requests — they may show malformed prompts from our side that produce higher compute.
[04:08] Marcus: we'll redact user data but share headers and sizes, yes.
[04:12] Priya: that'd be helpful. regarding retries, if we change retry policy and increase client timeout, is there a risk of longer tail latencies for normal users?
[04:20] Marcus: a small risk, but noise will be better than hard errors. and with jitter it spreads retries. plus we'll bump cache and that reduces cold-paths.
[04:29] Lina: action plan to be concrete: Marcus will collect logs/correlation IDs; Lina will bump rate limits; Priya will run spike tests; Tom will check ingress and retry config.
[04:39] Priya: yes, i'll run the tests once we get the script.
[04:42] Marcus: i'll upload the logs and recommended retry config.
[04:46] Lina: i'll send a note to infra to temporary rate bump now, and follow up with the SLA and any pricing implication, small one-time fee maybe.
[04:55] Maya: will that affect billing?
[04:56] Lina: for POC we'll waive overage for this mitigation, but if you want sustained higher capacity we'll need to discuss Dedicated or reserved capacity.
[05:05] Priya: understood.
[05:07] Tom: what about escalation — if the errors persist after these steps what's the path?
[05:11] Marcus: we'll schedule a deep-dive with Redwood infra and model runtime team, propose a maintenance window if needed to change node sizing or rolling restarts.
[05:20] Maya: ok. can we get a tentative date if needed?
[05:23] Lina: we'll decide by 2026-03-26 whether to escalate, based on spike results.
[05:28] Priya: sounds good. small nit — sometimes agent names in your logs come back as weird strings, makes analysis slower. is there a mapping table?
[05:36] Marcus: yes we have a correlation table and i'll include it; some auto-transcription or naming from edge can be off.
[05:41] Priya: perfect.
[05:43] Lina: ok final recap: we'll share logs, you'll run tests, we'll bump rate limit and tune retry/backoff, we'll monitor dashboards and reconvene if error rate stays >1%. any other items?
[05:55] Maya: can you also share suggested client SDK changes and sample code snippet?
[05:59] Marcus: yep i'll put a snippet for python and node with backoff and jitter.
[06:03] Lina: great. let's confirm owners in a follow-up email. thanks all.
[06:07] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll get those correlation IDs and run the tests.
[06:11] Tom: thanks.
[06:13] Maya: bye.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings and small tag swaps, timestamps approximate. Links shared during call: https://redwood.example.com/poc-dashboard (dashboard), https://redwood.example.com/retry-guidance (retry snippet), spreadsheet link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/poctests (results sheet).

End of transcript.
